about.title: Review: Find and Say Any Letter
about.length_note: About 12 minutes: this class reviews all 26 letters in small groups, then looks at look-alike letters, real words and a self-check. Each practice step can be paused, so it can be split into two sittings if tired. The one-idea-at-a-time steps stay the same either way.

say.text: Hello, and welcome to the last class. Today we use everything you have learned: find a letter, say its name and sound, and give a word for it.

show.text: Review: Find and Say Any Letter

say.text: First, a reminder. Every letter has two looks: upper case, which is big, and lower case, which is small. They are the same letter with the same name.

show.text: Upper case: A  B  G  M  R | Lower case: a  b  g  m  r

ask.q: Which pair shows the same letter in upper and lower case?
ask.why: G and g are two looks of one letter. The other pairs are two different letters.

say.text: Next, each letter has a name and a sound. The name is what we call it. The sound is what it says at the start of a word. B is called 'bee' and says 'buh', as in ball.

show.text: B b: name 'bee', sound 'buh', word ball

ask.q: Which sound do you hear at the start of the word ball?
ask.why: Ball starts with the 'buh' sound, which is the sound of the letter B.

say.text: So for any letter, we say three things: its name, its sound, and a familiar word. For A: 'ay', the sound 'a', and apple. Address works too.

show.text: A a: name 'ay' | sound 'a' | words: apple, address

say.text: Let us try it with K. Its name is 'kay' and its sound is 'kuh'. Two grown-up words for K are keys and kitchen.

show.text: K k: name 'kay' | sound 'kuh' | words: keys, kitchen

ask.q: Which word starts with the 'kuh' sound of K?
ask.why: Keys starts with K. The other words start with different letters.

say.text: Now random practice. Look at each letter, then say its name, its sound and a word. Pause the lesson and take your time.

show.text: g   T   m   R   a   K

say.text: Here is one set of answers. Check yours. g is 'jee', 'guh', grapes. T is 'tee', 'tuh', table. m is 'em', 'mm', moon. R is 'ar', 'rr', rain. Your words may differ, and that is fine.

show.text: g: grapes | T: table | m: moon | R: rain | a: apple | K: keys

ask.q: Which word goes with the letter m?
ask.why: Moon starts with the 'mm' sound, which is the sound of m.

say.text: Some letters look alike, so go slowly. Start with b and d. In b, you read the stick first, then the bump. In d, the bump comes first, then the stick.

show.text: b: stick first, bump second, 'buh', ball | d: bump first, stick second, 'duh', dog

ask.q: In the letter d, what comes first when you read left to right?
ask.why: In d the bump is on the left, so it comes first. The stick is on the right.

say.text: Another pair is p and q. Both have a tail that goes down. In p the bump is on the right, and it says 'puh', as in pig. In q the bump is on the left. It says 'kwuh', as in queen.

show.text: p: tail down, bump on the right, 'puh', pig | q: tail down, bump on the left, 'kwuh', queen

ask.q: Which letter has a tail down and a bump on the right?
ask.why: The letter p has its bump on the right. In q the bump is on the left.

say.text: The last look-alikes are capital I and small l. Capital I is 'eye' and says 'ih', as in ink. Small l is 'el' and says 'luh', as in lamp. In some print they look almost the same, so read the whole word.

ask.q: Which letter makes the 'luh' sound at the start of lamp?
ask.why: Lamp starts with l. The letter I makes a different sound, 'ih'.

say.text: Now let us find letters in real words. Take the name Sam. It has three letters: a big S, then a and m. Say each sound: 'sss', 'a', 'mm'.

ask.q: What is the first letter of the name Sam?
ask.why: Sam starts with a big S, which says 'sss'.

say.text: Now a word you see on letters and forms: address. It starts with a, and some letters repeat. Touch each letter and say its name.

show.text: a d d r e s s

ask.q: How many times does the letter d appear in the word address?
ask.why: Address is spelled a, d, d, r, e, s, s. The letter d is in the second and third places, so it appears twice.

say.text: Last step: mark how you did. Put the letters that felt easy in one list, and the letters that need another go in a second list. That is how you learn what to practise.

show.text: Easy: letters I said quickly | Another go: letters I want to see again

ask.q: Is it all right to put a letter in the 'another go' list?
ask.right: Yes, it just means you will look at it again.
wrong: No, every letter must be easy today.
Only if you got it wrong three times.
No, it means you cannot learn it.
ask.why: Everyone has letters that need more time. The list simply shows where to practise next.

say.text: Well done. You have met all 26 letters in upper and lower case, with names, sounds and words. Come back to your 'another go' list whenever you like.

show.text: A to Z: you can find and say any letter

notes.topic: Marking easy letters and letters for another go
